title: The Mountain Transformation and Real Greatness
paragraphs: §The Messiah

Jesus really emphasized his point, saying, "Listen, this isn't just some future dream. Some of you standing right here are actually going to see it happen, see God's kingdom arrive for real, with all its power."
§In a Light-Radiant Cloud

Sure enough, six days later, three of them totally saw it. Jesus took Peter, James, and John and hiked them up a super tall mountain. Right before their eyes, his whole appearance transformed from the inside out. His clothes were super bright, practically glowing white—like no laundry detergent could ever get them that white. Then, Elijah and Moses just showed up, chilling and talking with Jesus.

Peter cut in, "Teacher, this is an awesome moment! Let's build three little shelters (like tents or booths)—one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah." He just said it without even thinking, because they were all totally blown away by what they were seeing.
Just then, a super bright, glowing cloud covered them, and then a voice boomed from inside the cloud: "This is my Son, whom I love so much. Listen to him!"
The next minute, the disciples were looking around, rubbing their eyes, and all they saw was Jesus, just Jesus.

As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus made them promise to keep it a secret. "Don't tell a single soul what you saw. After the Son of Man rises from the dead, then you're free to talk." That really puzzled them, and they wondered what on earth "rising from the dead" even meant.
Meanwhile, they were asking, "Why do the religious scholars (the experts in Jewish law) say that Elijah has to come first?"

Jesus replied, "Elijah does come first and gets everything ready for the Son of Man to arrive. But they treated this Elijah like dirt, much like they will treat the Son of Man, who, according to the Scriptures, will suffer terribly and be treated with total disrespect."
§There Are No Ifs

When they got back down the mountain to the other disciples, they saw a huge crowd around them, and the religious scholars were grilling them with questions. As soon as the people in the crowd saw Jesus, they got super excited and ran to greet him. Jesus asked, "What's going on? Why all the chaos?"

A man from the crowd answered, "Teacher, I brought my son to you. He can't speak because a demon has made him mute. Whenever it grabs him, it throws him to the ground. He foams at the mouth, grinds his teeth, and goes stiff as a board. I asked your disciples, hoping they could get rid of it, but they couldn't."

Jesus said, "Seriously, what's up with this generation? You have no sense of God! How many times do I have to explain these things? How much longer do I have to put up with this? Bring the boy here." So they brought him. When the demon saw Jesus, it immediately threw the boy into a seizure, making him writhe on the ground and foam at the mouth.
Jesus asked the boy's father, "How long has this been happening?"

"Ever since he was a little kid," the father answered. "Many times it throws him into fire or into the river to try and kill him. If you can do anything, please do it. Have some compassion and help us!"
Jesus responded, "'If'? There are no 'ifs' for people who believe. Anything can happen!"
No sooner had Jesus said that than the father cried out, "Then I believe! Help me with my doubts!"

Seeing that the crowd was growing fast, Jesus gave the evil spirit its orders: "You spirit that keeps him from speaking and hearing, I command you—Get out of him, and stay out!" The spirit screamed and thrashed around a lot, then it left. The boy was so pale he looked like a corpse, so people started saying, "He's dead."
But Jesus took his hand and helped him up. The boy stood up.
After they arrived back home, his disciples cornered Jesus and asked, "Why couldn't we get that demon out?"
He answered, "There's no way to get rid of this kind of demon except by prayer."

Leaving there, they traveled through Galilee. Jesus didn't want anyone to know where they were because he wanted to teach his disciples. He told them, "The Son of Man is about to be betrayed to people who want nothing to do with God. They will murder him. But three days after his murder, he will rise, alive."
They didn't really understand what he was talking about, but they were too scared to ask him about it.
§So You Want First Place?
They arrived in Capernaum. When he was safely at home, he asked them, "What were you guys arguing about on the road?"
The silence was deafening—they had been arguing with each other over who among them was the greatest.
He sat down and called the Twelve (his main disciples) over. "So you want first place? Then you need to take the last place. Be the servant of everyone."

He put a child in the middle of the room. Then, holding the little one in his arms, he said, "Whoever welcomes one of these children just like I do, welcomes me. And even more than me—they welcome God who sent me."
John spoke up, "Teacher, we saw a guy using your name to cast out demons, and we stopped him because he wasn't part of our group."

Jesus wasn't pleased. "Don't stop him. No one can use my name to do something good and powerful, and then immediately turn around and trash me. If he's not against us, he's on our side. Seriously, anyone who just gives you a cup of water in my name is with us. You can count on God noticing that."

"On the other hand, if you cause one of these simple, childlike believers to stumble, bullying them or taking advantage of their innocent trust, you'll soon wish you hadn't. You'd be better off dropped in the middle of the lake with a huge stone (a millstone) tied around your neck."

"If your hand or your foot gets in God's way, chop it off and throw it away! You're better off maimed or lame and alive than having two hands and two feet and ending up godless in a furnace of eternal fire. And if your eye distracts you from God, pull it out and throw it away! You're better off one-eyed and alive than having perfect vision and ending up in the fire of hell."
"Everyone's going through a refining fire sooner or later, but you'll be well-preserved, protected from the eternal flames. Be preservatives yourselves. Preserve the peace."
